title: Frozen in Time: How a Physics Foundation Model Forgets Under Sim-to-Real Adaptation
abstract: arXiv:2610.40857v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Scientific foundation models (SciFMs) have achieved remarkable performance on a wide range of PDEs, including the ability to efficiently adapt to unseen data distributions with additional finetuning. As with all neural architectures, finetuning such models comes with the risk of catastrophic forgetting, whereby adapting to new tasks degrades prior knowledge of the model. We study catastrophic forgetting in Walrus-1.3B, a SciFM for continuum dynamics, over the course of a two-stage sim-to-real adaptation: first finetuning on simulated flow around a cylinder and then adapting to experimental data of the same system. We find that finetuning on the simulations rapidly degrades rollout performance on the original pretraining datasets, with one-step errors increasing up to 35x after just 20 epochs. translated_abstract: 科学基础模型（SciFMs）在广泛的偏微分方程（PDE）上取得了卓越的性能，包括能够通过额外的微调高效地适应未见过的数据分布。与所有神经架构一样，对此类模型进行微调伴随着灾难性遗忘的风险，即适应新任务会降低模型先前掌握的知识。我们研究了Walrus-1.3B——一个用于连续介质动力学的科学基础模型——在两阶段仿真到真实适配过程中的灾难性遗忘：首先在圆柱绕流的模拟数据上进行微调，然后适应同一系统的实验数据。我们发现，在模拟数据上的微调迅速降低了模型在原始预训练数据集上的滚动预测性能，仅经过20个训练周期后，单步误差增加了高达35倍。随后对真实数据的适应进一步削弱了在模拟任务上的性能。我们刻画了遗忘的潜在驱动因素，例如……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 研究发现，物理基础模型Walrus-1.3B在仿真到真实的两阶段微调过程中会发生严重的灾难性遗忘，仅20个训练周期后单步误差即增加高达35倍。
en_tdlr: This study reveals that the physics foundation model Walrus-1.3B suffers severe catastrophic forgetting during two-stage sim-to-real finetuning, with one-step errors increasing up to 35x after just 20 epochs.
